title: الجدل والإقناع
subtitle: Inversion and cleft sentences
intro: Two speakers can say the same thing, and one sounds forgettable while the other sounds unanswerable. The difference is usually emphasis — which English builds with inversion and cleft sentences.متحدّثان يقولان الشيء نفسه، فيبدو أحدهما عابراً والآخر لا يُردّ عليه. والفرق في الغالب هو التوكيد، وتبنيه الإنجليزيّة بالقلب والجمل المُركَّزة.
goals: I can emphasise any part of a sentence deliberately
I can use inversion after negative adverbials
I can build and defend an argument in English
I can hear stress carrying meaning in real speech

days.title: Inversion and cleft sentences
days.subtitle: putting the emphasis exactly where you want it

blocks.title: It-cleft: spotlight one element
blocks.html:
It + be + the element + that / who …

Neutral: Samir sent the email on Tuesday.

It was Samir who sent the email. — not anyone else
It was the email that Samir sent. — not the report
It was on Tuesday that Samir sent it. — not Monday

One sentence, three completely different arguments. This is the most useful structure in any debate.جملةٌ واحدة وثلاث حججٍ مختلفة تماماً. أنفع تركيبٍ في أيّ نقاش.

blocks.title: What-cleft: delay the point
blocks.html:
What … is / was … — builds tension, then delivers.

What surprised me was how quickly they agreed.
What we need is a clear deadline.
What he did was ignore every warning.

Also: The reason (why) … is that … / All I want is …

Native speakers use this constantly in speech. It gives the listener a second to prepare for the important part.تُؤخّر النقطة المهمّة فتُهيّئ السامع لها. يستعملها الناطقون الأصليّون باستمرار في الكلام.

blocks.title: Inversion after negative adverbials
blocks.html:
Start with a negative adverbial and the sentence inverts like a question:

Never have I seen such a weak argument.
Rarely does a policy survive its first year.
Not only did they refuse, they also complained.
At no point was the risk mentioned.
Under no circumstances should you sign it.

Others: Seldom, Little, No sooner … than, Hardly … when, Only after, Only then

⚠️ Formal and emphatic. One per paragraph is powerful; three is theatre.ابدأ بظرفٍ منفيّ فينقلب ترتيب الجملة كالسؤال. أسلوبٌ رسميّ قويّ: واحدةٌ في الفقرة قوّة، وثلاثٌ تمثيل.

blocks.title: Stress: the invisible grammar
blocks.html:
In speech, emphasis is often carried by the voice alone:

I didn't say he stole it. — someone else said it
I didn't say he stole it. — someone else stole it
I didn't say he stole it. — he borrowed it
I didn't say he stole it. — he stole something else

Seven words, seven meanings. When you watch films, the stressed word is the meaning.سبع كلماتٍ وسبعة معانٍ، والفارق هو النبر وحده. حين تشاهد فيلماً فالكلمة المنبورة هي المعنى.

days.title: Reading: why winning an argument changes nothing
days.subtitle: نصّ + استنتاج المعنى من السياق

blocks.title: Why Winning an Argument Changes Nothing
blocks.titleAr: لماذا لا يغيّر الفوز بالجدل شيئاً
blocks.en:
Anyone who has won a public argument knows the strange silence that follows. You produced better evidence, you dismantled the other position, and the person opposite you believes exactly what they believed before. What the research suggests is that this is the normal outcome, not the exception.

The reason is not stupidity. People hold positions for reasons that are partly social, and a defeat in public raises the cost of changing your mind rather than lowering it. Never does anyone enjoy being corrected in front of colleagues. The better your argument, the more expensive their retreat becomes.

What does work is slower and less satisfying. Asking someone to explain the mechanism of their own position — not to defend it, but to describe how it would actually work — reliably softens confidence. So does conceding a real point early, which signals that you are not simply collecting wins. It is trust, not logic, that moves people, and trust is built in the parts of a conversation nobody remembers.

None of this means evidence is useless. It means evidence persuades in private, over time, and usually after the argument is over. The people most skilled at changing minds are rarely the ones who look most impressive doing it.
blocks.ar:
كلّ من فاز بجدلٍ علنيّ يعرف ذلك الصمت الغريب الذي يليه. فقد قدّمتَ أدلّةً أفضل، وفكّكتَ موقف الطرف الآخر، وهو يؤمن تماماً بما كان يؤمن به قبل ذلك. وما توحي به الأبحاث أنّ هذه هي النتيجة المعتادة لا الاستثناء.

والسبب ليس الغباء. فالناس يتّخذون مواقف لأسبابٍ اجتماعيّةٍ جزئيّاً، والهزيمة العلنيّة ترفع كلفة تغيير الرأي بدل أن تخفضها. ولا يستمتع أحدٌ قطّ بأن يُصحَّح أمام زملائه. وكلّما كانت حجّتك أقوى صار تراجعه أبهظ.

وما يفلح فعلاً أبطأ وأقلّ إرضاءً. فأن تطلب من أحدٍ شرح آليّة موقفه — لا أن يدافع عنه بل أن يصف كيف سيعمل فعلاً — يخفّف ثقته على نحوٍ موثوق. وكذلك التسليم بنقطةٍ حقيقيّةٍ مبكّراً، فهو يشير إلى أنّك لا تجمع انتصارات. فالثقة لا المنطق هي ما يحرّك الناس، والثقة تُبنى في أجزاء المحادثة التي لا يتذكّرها أحد.

ولا يعني شيءٌ من هذا أنّ الأدلّة عديمة الفائدة، بل يعني أنّها تُقنع على انفراد، وعبر الوقت، وبعد انتهاء الجدل عادةً. وأمهر الناس في تغيير العقول نادراً ما يكونون أكثرهم إبهاراً وهم يفعلون ذلك.

days.subtitle: Conceding, challenging and holding the floor

blocks.title: Conceding without losing
blocks.html:
That's a fair point, but … — the standard move
I'll grant you that. What I'd add is …
You're right about X. Where I differ is Y.
I take your point — my concern is still …
That may well be true, and it doesn't change …

The structure is always the same: concede something real, then pivot. Conceding nothing makes everything you say sound like defence.البنية واحدة دائماً: سلّم بشيءٍ حقيقيّ ثمّ انعطف. ومن لا يسلّم بشيءٍ يبدو كلامه كلّه دفاعاً.

blocks.title: Challenging and holding the floor
blocks.html:
Challenging:
What's the evidence for that?
How would that actually work? — the mechanism question
Is that true across the board, or just here?
I'm not sure that follows. — logic, politely

Holding the floor when interrupted:
If I could just finish the thought …
Let me get to the point and then it's yours.
Hang on — one more sentence.عباراتٌ للاعتراض المهذّب، وأخرى للاحتفاظ بدورك في الكلام حين يقاطعك أحد.

blocks.title: 🚫 لا تقل هذا
blocks.html:
❌ I am not agree → ✅ I don't agree
❌ You are wrong in this point → ✅ I'd question that / I'm not sure that's right
❌ In my point of view → ✅ From my point of view / In my view
❌ Let me explain you → ✅ Let me explain
❌ This is not logic → ✅ This isn't logical
❌ I have a different opinion than you → ✅ I see it differently
❌ Actually to mean «in fact, currently» → ✅ at the moment / currently

actually in English means «in reality, contrary to what you think» — it contradicts, it does not update.انتبه: actually بالإنجليزية تعني «في الواقع، خلافاً لما تظنّ» — فهي تناقض ولا تعني «حاليّاً».

blocks.title: The task
blocks.prompt:
Argue for a position you actually hold, in 140–160 words. It must include:

• one it-cleft and one what-cleft
• one inversion after a negative adverbial
• one genuine concession to the other side
• one direct answer to the strongest counterargument
• at least four words from this unitحاجّ لموقفٍ تؤمن به فعلاً في ١٤٠–١٦٠ كلمة، بجملة it-cleft وأخرى what-cleft، وقلبٍ بعد ظرفٍ منفيّ، وتسليمٍ حقيقيّ للطرف الآخر، وردٍّ مباشر على أقوى حجّةٍ مضادّة، وأربع كلماتٍ من الوحدة.
phrases: It is not X but Y that …
That may well be true, and it doesn't change …
blocks.model:
What I'd argue is that schools should teach statistics instead of advanced algebra. Not because algebra is useless, but because almost nobody uses it, while everybody is shown numbers designed to persuade them.

It is not mathematical ability but statistical literacy that decides whether a person can read a news chart, a medical leaflet or a loan agreement. Never has the volume of misleading data been higher, and never have people been less equipped to question it.

I'll concede the obvious point: algebra trains abstract reasoning, and statistics taught badly becomes a list of formulas nobody understands. That is a real risk.

The strongest counterargument is that universities require algebra. That may well be true, and it doesn't change the fact that we are optimising a whole school system for the minority who will study engineering.

The bottom line is that we teach the maths that is easy to test, not the maths that is easy to need.
blocks.modelAr:
ما أحاجّ به هو أنّ على المدارس تدريس الإحصاء بدل الجبر المتقدّم. لا لأنّ الجبر عديم الفائدة، بل لأنّ أحداً لا يكاد يستعمله، بينما يُعرض على الجميع أرقامٌ صُمّمت لإقناعهم.

ليست القدرة الرياضيّة بل الثقافة الإحصائيّة هي ما يحدّد إن كان المرء قادراً على قراءة رسمٍ إخباريّ أو نشرةٍ دوائيّة أو عقد قرض. ولم يكن حجم البيانات المضلّلة أعلى ممّا هو عليه قطّ، ولم يكن الناس أقلّ تجهيزاً للتشكيك فيها.

وأسلّم بالنقطة البديهيّة: الجبر يدرّب التفكير المجرّد، والإحصاء إن دُرّس بسوءٍ صار قائمة صيغٍ لا يفهمها أحد. وهذه مخاطرةٌ حقيقيّة.

وأقوى حجّةٍ مضادّة أنّ الجامعات تشترط الجبر. وقد يكون ذلك صحيحاً تماماً، ولا يغيّر أنّنا نضبط نظاماً مدرسيّاً بأكمله لأجل أقلّيّةٍ ستدرس الهندسة.

والخلاصة أنّنا ندرّس الرياضيّات التي يسهل اختبارها لا التي يسهل أن يُحتاج إليها.
checklist: I used an it-cleft (It is … that …)
I inverted after a negative adverbial (Never has / Not only did …)
I conceded one real point, not a fake one
I named and answered the strongest counterargument
I used at least four unit words (premise, concede, misleading, counterargument …)
I wrote 'I don't agree', never 'I am not agree'
I ended with a clear bottom line

items.task: سجّل خمس جملٍ فيها قلبٌ أو تركيز، كما سمعتها.

items.d: ابحث عن مقابلات «60 Minutes» — أسئلةٌ حادّة وردودٌ متحوّطة
items.task: احصِ كم مرّة سلّم ضيفٌ بنقطةٍ قبل أن يعترض.

items.d: ابحث عن «The Ezra Klein Show» — خلافٌ مهذّب ومطوّل
items.task: استمع عشرين دقيقة، واكتب ثلاث عباراتٍ للاعتراض المهذّب.
اقرأ «I never said that» بأربع نبراتٍ مختلفة، وميّز المعاني الأربعة.
